issues.evidence: Tibetan 'ཡིད་ཕེབས' (Sanskrit viśvasta) is glossed by bo-gyaltsab 5-79 as 'སྙིང་ཐག་པ་ནས་ཡིད་ཕེབས་པ' (heartfelt, winning trust) and by bo-kunpal as speech that accords with the listener's inclination; 'pleasant' is the separate item 'ཡིད་དུ་འོང་བ' already rendered 'मनोहारी', so 'सुखद' duplicates it and loses the sense of sincerity/trust.
Line 2 of the Hindi ends with an ideographic full stop (U+3002) instead of a danda or Latin full stop; a typographic error, meaning unaffected.

Tibetan 'འདི་དང་གཞན་དུ་ཡང་' means 'in this and other (worlds/lives)'; bo-gyaltsab 5-87 explains 'ཚེ་རབས་འདི་དང་གཞན་དུ་ཡང་' and bo-kunpal 'འཇིག་རྟེན་འདི་དང་འཇིག་རྟེན་གཞན་དུ་ཡང་'. The Hindi leaves 'अन्य' without its noun, so it reads as an unspecified 'other'.
